plan: This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. Since payment is based on the second-highest bid (not what I bid), bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever profitable (value exceeds second-highest bid) and never overpay. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if I win; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. I will bid my true value of $35.

This is a second-price auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do - it maximizes expected profit. Bidding higher than value risks winning at a loss; bidding lower reduces chances of winning profitable auctions without changing the price paid when I do win. With no prior history to adjust for, I'll bid exactly my value of $32.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of competitors' behavior. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down—overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing a profitable auction. With a value of $48, I will bid exactly $48 to maximize expected profit.
